en.html:
Tearing up through the sky toward its highest point—never once had I found that pleasant. The skin rose in fear instead. Bottomless depths. An end beyond every end. A place where there was nothing. The unknown. And into that I was driving myself. Cold dread went straight into the spine.

The Gattari's thrust was a little lower than usual. Altitude was not coming as quickly as it should. Today even the sky was sluggish.

Caloric reserves insufficient, apparently. Even so, an ordinary opponent should not have been beyond us. Should not...

Cheerful metal-echo in my ears. Failure complained of, disappointment entirely absent. The old fellow had missed his kill and was discussing it as though the chai required a little more ginger.

Hasso. Sword beside the body, parallel to it. Thrusting from there was uncommon in aerial combat. High-speed warrior, little sword-point—meeting the two correctly was far harder than hitting with the edge.

Lekin lag gaya toh. If it landed, all that tremendous force arrived in one point only. Armor laughing at cannon shells became paper. The laugh could remain unfinished inside.

Probably no warrior could withstand a perfect thrust. Ordinarily, then, a desperate reversal from a losing position.

Ordinarily. This uncle had brought it out while winning.

　故に、これが用いられる局面は劣勢からの起死回生
というのが定石。
